departments.name: Canadian Natural Gas Pipelines (加拿大天然气管道)
departments.description: Operates the NGTL System (24,631 km), Canadian Mainline (14,101 km), Foothills (1,237 km) and other Canadian gas transmission assets. Generates approximately $3.7 billion in annual comparable EBITDA.

departments.name: U.S. Natural Gas Pipelines (美国天然气管道)
departments.description: Operates Columbia Gas (18,768 km), ANR Pipeline (15,075 km), Columbia Gulf (5,419 km), Great Lakes, GTN, Crossroads and other U.S. gas transmission systems. Largest segment by EBITDA at approximately $4.9 billion annually.

departments.name: Mexico Natural Gas Pipelines (墨西哥天然气管道)
departments.description: Operates a network of approximately 3,500 km of natural gas pipelines across Mexico including Guadalajara, Mazatlan, Tamazunchale, Topolobampo and the new Southeast Gateway Pipeline (715 km). Transports approximately 20% of Mexico's total gas demand.

departments.name: Power and Energy Solutions (电力与能源解决方案)
departments.description: Manages approximately 4,650 MW of power generation capacity including Bruce Power nuclear (48.4% interest, 6,400 MW total), natural gas cogeneration plants in Alberta and Quebec, and emerging solar and pumped storage projects.

recent_events.title: Southeast Gateway Pipeline enters commercial service
recent_events.description: TC Energy commenced toll collection on the 715-km Southeast Gateway Pipeline offshore Mexico, completed approximately 13% under budget at US$3.9 billion. The pipeline connects Tuxpan, Veracruz to Coatzacoalcos and Paraiso, strengthening energy security in southeastern Mexico.
recent_events.impact: Strengthens TC Energy's position as the largest natural gas pipeline operator in Mexico; supports Mexico's plan to add 8.5 GW of new gas-fired generation capacity

recent_events.title: Coastal GasLink pipeline celebrates commercial in-service
recent_events.description: TC Energy hosted a celebration in Vancouver marking the completion and commercial in-service of the 670-km Coastal GasLink pipeline feeding LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C. The project cost an estimated $14.5 billion, unlocking Canadian LNG exports to global markets.
recent_events.impact: Enables Canada's first major LNG export terminal, supplying Asian markets with up to 14 million tonnes annually of LNG

recent_events.title: TC Energy reports record 2025 full-year results
recent_events.description: TC Energy reported full-year 2025 comparable EBITDA of $11.0 billion (up 9% YoY), net income of $3.6 billion, and 15 delivery records across its pipeline systems. Board approved a 3.2% dividend increase, marking 26 consecutive years of dividend growth. 2026 comparable EBITDA outlook raised to $11.6-$11.8 billion.
recent_events.impact: Demonstrates resilient financial performance post-South Bow spinoff; confirms growth trajectory with $6 billion annual net capital expenditure capacity through 2030

recent_events.title: Coastal GasLink Phase 2 commercial agreements signed with LNG Canada
recent_events.description: TC Energy signed commercial agreements with LNG Canada to advance the second phase of the Coastal GasLink pipeline, establishing a comprehensive commercial framework. The agreement represents a significant step toward expanding Canadian LNG export capacity to Asian markets.
recent_events.impact: Positions TC Energy as a critical enabler of Canada's LNG expansion to Asia-Pacific markets, potentially doubling LNG export capacity from the West Coast

recent_events.title: CEO Poirier advocates for North American energy infrastructure investment
recent_events.description: TC Energy CEO Francois Poirier appeared on CNBC Squawk Box discussing global energy markets, the impact of the Iran war on energy supply, and North America's critical need for energy infrastructure investment. He emphasized data center-driven power demand and LNG export growth as key demand drivers.
recent_events.impact: Positions TC Energy as a thought leader in North American energy policy and infrastructure development discourse

core_business: TC Energy Corporation (TSX:TRP, NYSE:TRP) is North America's leading energy infrastructure company, operating a natural gas pipeline network spanning approximately 94,000 kilometres (58,000 miles) across Canada, the United States and Mexico. The company transports over 30% of all natural gas consumed on the continent daily, making it the largest natural gas pipeline operator in North America. Following the October 2024 spinoff of its crude oil liquids pipelines business into South Bow Corporation, TC Energy focuses exclusively on three core segments: natural gas pipelines (generating approximately 87% of EBITDA), power and energy solutions, and natural gas storage. The company holds ownership interests in seven power generation facilities with a combined capacity of 4,650 MW, including a 48.4% stake in Bruce Power, the world's largest operating nuclear power plant. TC Energy reported comparable EBITDA of $11.0 billion in 2025, with 98% underpinned by rate-regulated or long-term take-or-pay contracts. Headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, the company employs approximately 6,500 people and has maintained dividend growth for 26 consecutive years. Its strategic assets include the NGTL System, Canadian Mainline, Columbia Gas, ANR Pipeline, Coastal GasLink, and the Southeast Gateway Pipeline in Mexico.
apec_stance: TC Energy高度关注亚太地区能源市场,其CEO Francois Poirier多次公开表示加拿大有望成为亚洲最大的液化天然气(LNG)供应国。公司通过Coastal GasLink管道向LNG Canada供应天然气,该终端于2025年投产后年出口能力达1400万吨,主要面向日本、韩国和中国等APEC经济体。2026年3月,TC Energy与LNG Canada签署了Coastal GasLink第二阶段商业协议,进一步扩大加拿大西海岸对亚太地区的LNG出口能力。Poirier强调,中东冲突和美国贸易紧张局势凸显了加拿大向亚洲增加LNG出口的紧迫性,呼吁加拿大政府采取更有力的政策支持LNG基础设施建设。TC Energy在墨西哥运营的天然气管道网络(包括Southeast Gateway管道)同样服务于APEC成员国墨西哥的能源安全,输送约占该国20%的天然气需求。公司主张北美能源一体化和跨太平洋能源贸易自由化,认为APEC框架下的能源基础设施投资对区域能源安全至关重要。
